bull.probability_evidence: Every current multiple sits below its 5y minimum (P/E 8.8x vs 10.8x floor; EV/EBITDA 11.7x vs 13.1x floor; P/B 0.9x vs 1.1x floor, factsheet-2026-10-09.md Valuation table RA) while ROIC (7.7%) and ROE (9.8%) are flat over five years (factsheet Quality table RA) -- the de-rating is rate-driven, not fundamental. The overlay's macro_bull path (real yields rolling over on a confirmed Fed easing path, research/VICI/2026-10-09-macro.md) is the trigger, but probability is held at 0.2 because the overlay carries primary weight with a moderate tilt toward bear: DFII10 is +0.49pp/1m and +0.61pp/3m with the trend still rising, not stabilizing (same macro.md), arguing against a full re-rating to the 48.02 fair-value bull case.

target_band.cite: Fact sheet Valuation table (RA; peers P:GLPI,P:EPR,P:O,P:NNN): peer-median-implied prices from the current price $22.79 scaled by each multiple vs its peer median: P/E 8.8x->peer 18.6x implies $48.17; EV/EBITDA 11.7x->peer 14.1x implies $27.46; EV/Sales 10.4x->peer 12.6x implies $27.61; P/B 0.9x->peer 1.8x implies $45.58 (factsheet-2026-10-09.md Valuation table). Half-spread ($48.17-$27.46)/2=$10.36 / average implied price $37.21 = 27.8%, which exceeds the mc-inputs.json blended residual volatility of 16.56% (regression.residual_vol.blended); capped at 16.50% (just under that measured ceiling) per the montecarlo.py bound. The fact sheet's own fair-value table uses a single method (P/FFO proxy; NAV is [data unavailable]), so this cross-multiple disagreement is the only valuation-anchor spread available and is applied identically to all three scenarios.

base.probability_evidence: Net debt/EBITDA (site definition) has risen from 2.96x (FY21) to 4.82x TTM (factsheet Quality table RA) while the 10y real yield trend is still rising, not stabilizing (DFII10 +0.61pp/3m, research/VICI/2026-10-09-macro.md) -- a continued headwind, but ROIC (7.7%) and ROE (9.8%) are flat rather than deteriorating (factsheet Quality table RA), consistent with a partial re-rating (EV/EBITDA moving from 11.7x toward about 12.5x, still below the 13.1x 5y floor) rather than a full re-rating to fair value or a further breakdown. This modal path is weighted highest because it matches both the still-rising-but-not-extending macro tilt and flat (not falling) fundamentals.
